reaction: Dai, 63, a dam keeper for thirty-one years, separated, daughter near home. The panel reads like a stage direction: wait five seconds, then Invite conversation. Odd, but I want to talk to him before I hand him a trolley. Waiting five seconds.

Reason to act: a storm at 10:00, a storehouse of 180 boards and 120 ballast bags. Nora is on ballast, Sam on boards. I stopped at Dai, 63, the dam keeper, and wanted to talk first. I gave him a break, waited, pressed Invite conversation twice - each time it just repeats: spend a minute together first. A minute of what? Standing with him? I am not sure the minute has started. The clock runs about one game minute per real second.

Everyone has work now except Dai, who rests. Eight people in eight taps, each a little card: accountant, photographer, retired teacher whose spouse died. The cards are nice but they read like a form. The About panels for Dai and Sevim end with the same instruction sentence. Ballast looks like the bottleneck: 21 of 120.

Help explains it: a minute together, THEN a break, then five seconds, then Invite conversation. So I did it in the wrong order with Dai. The "minute together" - I still do not know what counts as together. Workshop hub can invite a local helper. People 8/10 - two more could come.
Dai has had his break and was just waiting. Boards for him, a comfortable trolley load. I will stay with him selected for a minute and see if that counts as together.

Dai said: I am tired, I need a break. I gave it at once - that is the kind of moment I want. But the storehouse is already affordable at 2:25 of 10:00; the storm feels far less threatening than the title said.

Dai opened up: "I kept a list of checks in my head... I liked being needed, so that was hard to admit." As an engineer that hits home - the temporary fix you keep because it makes you necessary. That one line made him a person. Offer a small collaboration is now enabled. I want to try it.

The collaboration: he writes an inspection card and leaves room for Nora to question it, but is not handing over the dam. That is a careful, honest sentence - he lets go a little, not all the way. I like that the game did not make him a reformed man. Now the storehouse: we have enough. Select builders, Storehouse, tap open ground.

Twice: "Choose open ground, away from cabins and delivered materials." On this phone the map is a thin strip behind the speed buttons. I cannot see any open ground, or where the cabins and materials are. I am guessing at spots.

Four taps, four times "Choose open ground". I have all the boards and bags, I know exactly what I want - put the storehouse down - and I cannot find ground on a strip of map the size of my thumb. And Nora says she is tired again, right after resting. I would close it here. Keeping on.

Fifth tap, just below the hub, worked: storehouse 0% complete, Nora and Sam preparing it. Relief, but it was luck not reading. Nora said she was tired and I sent her to build anyway - I feel a bit bad. Adding Dai would be a lot to ask of him.

Nora: she left out the easier grip because she preferred the simpler shape, and did not ask the user. Then she adds it back, still untested, and she and her brother are still distant. I like the honesty - did not ask the person who would use it is exactly my profession sin. But now I see the shape: confession, small fix, "still" unresolved. Same as Dai. Two in a row the same mould.

Sevim: she called a pupil lazy before learning he cared for a sick parent, and kept his exercise books, and never admitted it. That one is heavier. But it is the third confession in a row, all the same three beats. I begin to feel I am collecting confessions. This time I will not press Offer a small collaboration - I want to just let her have said it, and see if that is allowed.

Burak broke the mould - no confession, a folded card with a moving ferry inside, something that does not have to be useful. He leaves it unfinished on the shared table. I smiled at that. An accountant keeping the shared money separate from his hobby is a nice, quiet detail.

Sam, 18, who tests games: he copied another player description into a report and said he had checked it. That made me laugh and wince - a game tester confessing to a game tester. Confession number four out of five. Now the requested wide check (not my choice).

Wide check at 5:00 (requested): oh - there is a whole map. Prepared boards, ballast bags, meal crates, the hub, my storehouse with Sam in it, little people standing at piles. On the phone I saw none of it, just a strip. This is where I would have placed the storehouse in one tap. Tapped the Workshop hub by position and invited a helper for 35 meals. Going back to the phone now.

Nerys and her telescope - a dark corner of the courtyard, cannot promise clear skies. Gentle. Aylin, the helper, has joined. Storehouse 55% at 5:22, comfortably ahead. I like these people, but the loop is now fixed: they say I am tired, I give a break, wait five seconds, open About, invite, offer collaboration. A vending machine of small kind paragraphs. Nothing pulls against anything.

Dilek records kitchen sounds - the loose lid has a wonderful rattle, and she leaves voices out unless people agree. I like her. I leave the collaboration this time. Oskar is the last one I have not heard.

Oskar: a photo caption that made a volunteer look like they stayed through a storm, when they had sensibly gone home. That one is clever, given we are all working before a storm. Fifth confession. Everyone here has a small dishonesty and none of them touch each other. I wanted Dai and Nora to meet over that inspection card - he left room for her to question it - but nothing happens between people.
I went back to Dai to talk again. Invite conversation just returned "I am tired. I need a break." One conversation per person and then the thread is closed? I wanted to ask him about his daughter.
Second placement try worked: Dai will prepare the guest cabin. Dai is tired and I sent him to build anyway; he did not object, so maybe fine. Now I wait and watch the storehouse finish.

"The storehouse is finished. The shared supplies are ready for the storm." At 6:51, three game hours early. One status line, no moment - nobody remarks on it, nobody gathers. The storm I worried about at the start never felt close. I will see what the storm itself brings; meanwhile I have nothing I need to do.

The storehouse is done, everyone has said their one thing, Nora is eating and then will wait. I would leave now - I understand it and there is nothing I need to do. Staying to see the storm at 10:00, three game hours, about three real minutes.

It says: The storm will arrive in two minutes. Finish the storehouse. But the line above says the storehouse is ready. Which is it? Also People went from 9/10 to 9/12 - did the cabin finish? Nobody told me.
I just keep tapping Rest when someone says they are tired. It is kind, but it is chores. Waiting for the storm to see if anything I did mattered.

That is it? The storm arrived, the supplies stayed dry, and the last words are Nora saying she will rest and Sam saying the building is finished. No scene of the rain, nothing about Dai or Burak or the guests. Relief, then flat. I want to see the tally.

9 people, 3 completed buildings. Three? I counted the storehouse and maybe the cabin. The game is over and I would leave here. My time is not up, so I will look at the title page to see if there is another way to play.

A longer day: eight fresh residents, a night, conversations and sleep. That sounds more like what I wanted - people with time. It is thirty minutes and I have maybe fourteen left, so I will not finish it. Starting anyway.

Fresh residents, it said - but it is Nora, Sam, Dai, Nerys again, the same eight names. Are they the same people who confided in me, or strangers with the same names? I do not know. There is Paper 4 now. Opening Travel, conversations and the day.

A wall of text. The framework fictional timetable, the current finite departure route supports the ten-minute chapter - I do not know what that means and I read it twice. But Invite two people to talk is exactly what I want. I will put Dilek and Burak together - kitchen sounds and a paper ferry.

Invited to talk about the supplies and the shared route. Oh - I wanted them to talk about themselves, not supplies. Dilek will consider it alongside her needs. Fine, I will give them time. Meanwhile someone should fetch ballast; we have 0.

Dilek and Burak talked and all I get is: They do not pass on an account of the supplies. Twice, mirrored. That is not a conversation, that is a form. But now Oskar and Sam are fighting over the narrow trolley route - finally a quarrel between people. Sam is 18, Oskar older I think. I will not make the boy yield first; let them talk.
A real quarrel appeared and it made me sit up, but their talk produced no words at all, and 7 of 120 ballast bags after an hour. I will ask Oskar to yield, not the boy, and see if anyone minds.

reaction: Oskar yields the shared trolley route after choosing to make room. Good, the route is open. He chose it, I only asked. But that was the whole quarrel - one line, no word from Sam, no thanks. And Sam keeps inspecting the yard cache over and over. Ballast still 7. The longer day is mostly a log scrolling past me.

On the phone the map is a sliver; the people are three dots under the speed buttons. Everything I do is in the text panel. Route is open, so Oskar can carry ballast now - tapping Ballast bags by position.

Oskar tells me he faked a photo caption - a volunteer staying through a storm who had sensibly gone home. That is a nice line, and fitting the day. But I think he confessed something like this in the short chapter too; I am not sure if it is the same words. Fresh residents, same confessions? It lands softer the second time. And it is buried in a log under Sam inspects the yard cache, four times.
Oskar told me something real once, then went back to resting while Sam inspects the cache for the fifth time. 27 of 120 bags, nine hours to go, and I am reading a log, not a place.

I am stopping here. I pressed I am stopping in Feedback; it filled the note box with those words by itself. I typed nothing and did not submit. The short chapter ended cleanly - supplies dry - but flatly. The longer day gave me one real quarrel and Oskar faked caption, then a log of Sam inspecting the cache. I understand it; I just have nothing I want to do here. I would not leave it running. I might come back another evening on desktop for the longer day, if people talked to each other in words and not reports.
